name: Toxiproxy
what_it_is: A TCP proxy framework written in Go by Shopify that intercepts test connections and simulates adverse network conditions. Applications route traffic through it and a separate HTTP API controls which fault-injection 'toxics' are active.
components: toxiproxy-server (TCP proxy daemon, HTTP API on port 8474)
client libraries (Ruby, Go, Python, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Java, Haskell, Rust, Elixir)
measurement: Throughput ~1000 MB/s on MacBook Pro, ~2400 MB/s on high-end desktop
configuration: Proxy defined by: name, listen address, upstream address, enabled flag
Toxic defined by: name, type, stream direction (upstream/downstream), toxicity probability (0.0–1.0), type-specific attributes
Bulk proxy creation via POST /populate with JSON array
Configuration via JSON file or live HTTP API
fault_injection: latency — adds delay ± jitter (ms) to the stream
bandwidth — caps throughput to a given rate (KB/s)
slow_close — delays TCP socket closure by N ms
timeout — drops all data and closes connection after N ms (0 = indefinite hold)
reset_peer — sends TCP RST after optional timeout
slicer — fragments packets into smaller chunks with inter-chunk delay (µs)
limit_data — closes connection once a byte threshold is exceeded
modes: Development environment (manual toxic toggling via CLI or API)
CI/CD integration (programmatic API-driven fault scenarios per test)
Resiliency / chaos testing on non-production systems
constraints: Avoid listen ports in the Linux ephemeral range 32768–61000 to prevent port conflicts
MySQL default Unix-socket preference bypasses TCP proxy; socket must be disabled in MySQL config
Server v2.x client libraries are incompatible with server v1.x (breaking API change)
Not intended for production traffic interception — designed for test/CI environments only
docker_services: ghcr.io/shopify/toxiproxy (official image, exposes port 8474 for HTTP API plus user-defined proxy ports)
notable_absences: No built-in TLS/SSL termination or inspection — operates below the TLS layer
No docker-compose.yml in the upstream repository
No authentication on the HTTP management API — network-level access control required
